subject: Religious and Moral Education
source: RELIGIOUS AND MORAL EDUCATION CURRICULUM FOR PRIMARY SCHOOLS (BASIC I - 6), September 2019
teacher_guidance: Read aloud when needed. Accept oral responses in a familiar language. Assess knowledge of the curriculum's religious teaching rather than personal belief. Do not grade artistic skill. Never require an actual hospital or orphanage visit.

indicators.objective: Mention the names of some of the things God created.
indicators.content_standard_as_printed: BI. 1.1.1. Explain who the Creator is

skills.description: Name creations listed in the curriculum.
Recognise listed creations in short descriptions.
Represent and explain listed creations through speaking, drawing, modelling or rhyme.

misconceptions: Human-made objects are confused with the listed creations
A drawing or model is confused with the thing represented

questions.stem: Which is named in our lesson as something God created?
hints: Think about something that grows.
questions.explanation: The lesson lists trees among God's creations. Desks, pencils and buses are made by people.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Furniture is confused with a listed creation
distractor_misconceptions.2: A writing tool is confused with a listed creation
distractor_misconceptions.3: A vehicle is confused with a listed creation

questions.stem: Which group is named among God's creations in the lesson?
hints: Think about living creatures.
questions.explanation: Animals are explicitly listed. The other groups contain things made by people.

distractor_misconceptions.0: Containers are confused with living creations
distractor_misconceptions.2: Clothing is confused with living creations
distractor_misconceptions.3: Crafted objects are confused with living creations

questions.stem: Name the people group included among God's creations in our lesson.
hints: Think about you, your classmates and your family.
questions.explanation: You and your family are human beings. The curriculum lists humankind among God's creations.

questions.stem: Which water feature is named in the lesson?
hints: Choose the feature rather than something used to carry water.
questions.explanation: Rivers are listed among God's creations. Buckets, cups and taps are human-made objects.

distractor_misconceptions.0: A container is confused with a water feature
distractor_misconceptions.1: A drinking container is confused with a water feature
distractor_misconceptions.3: A water fitting is confused with a water feature

questions.stem: Which large land feature is listed among God's creations?
hints: Think about a high natural land feature.
questions.explanation: Mountains are named in the curriculum. Schools, walls and roads are built by people.

distractor_misconceptions.0: A building is confused with a land feature
distractor_misconceptions.1: A built barrier is confused with a land feature
distractor_misconceptions.2: A built route is confused with a land feature

questions.stem: A chart shows a tree beside a chair. Which one belongs to the lesson's list of God's creations?
hints: Recall the example that grows.
questions.explanation: Identify each object first. Trees are listed; a chair is a human-made object.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Furniture is confused with a listed creation
distractor_misconceptions.2: Different objects are given the same name

questions.stem: A picture shows a person. Which curriculum word names all people together?
hints: Think of the group name for people.
questions.explanation: One person belongs to the group called humankind. That group is named in the lesson.

questions.stem: Ama wants a picture of a listed water feature. Which should she choose?
hints: Choose a natural feature rather than a container.
questions.explanation: The sea is listed among God's creations. The other choices are containers made by people.

distractor_misconceptions.0: A cooking container is confused with the sea
distractor_misconceptions.2: A container is confused with a natural feature
distractor_misconceptions.3: A pouring container is confused with a natural feature

questions.stem: Your teacher says 'rivers and the sea'. Tell which kind of feature both examples are.
hints: Think about what both contain.
questions.explanation: Consider what the examples share. Both are water features in the lesson's list.

criteria.description: Identifies both as water features or places containing water.
Recognises both as listed creations.

questions.stem: A classroom chart shows a person, a tree and a mountain. Name all three.
hints: Point to each picture before naming it.
questions.explanation: Name each item separately. Each belongs to the curriculum's list of creations.

criteria.description: Names the person or human being.
Names the tree.
Names the mountain.

questions.stem: Kojo says a picture of the sea shows a river. Tell him the correct name when the teacher labels the picture 'sea'.
hints: Use the picture's label.
questions.explanation: Read or hear the label first. Use sea rather than replacing it with another listed water feature.

criteria.description: Uses the name sea.
Recognises sea and river as different names in the curriculum list.

questions.stem: Choose two items from this list that our lesson names as God's creations: mountain, pencil, animal, shoe.
hints: Separate living or natural things from manufactured objects.
questions.explanation: Check each item against the curriculum examples. Mountain and animal are included.

criteria.description: Selects mountain.
Selects animal without including pencil or shoe.

questions.stem: Draw one tree and one animal. Name each for your teacher.
hints: Plan two separate pictures.
questions.explanation: Represent the two requested creations. Explain each picture so meaning is clear.

criteria.description: Represents and names a tree.
Represents and names an animal.

questions.stem: Use safe modelling material to show a mountain. Tell what your model represents and connect it to our lesson.
hints: Think of the land feature you want to show.
questions.explanation: Make a representation, name it, and link it to the curriculum example.

criteria.description: Identifies the model as a mountain.
Links mountains to the lesson's list of God's creations.

questions.stem: Tell a partner about a picture containing people, trees and a river. Use the three correct names.
hints: Describe one part of the picture at a time.
questions.explanation: Name each represented creation. Connect all three names in a short description.

criteria.description: Correctly names people, trees and a river.
Gives a coherent description connecting the three.

questions.stem: Draw two different water features named in our lesson. Tell your teacher their names.
hints: Recall the two water examples in the curriculum.
questions.explanation: Choose the river and the sea. Explain the intended names rather than relying on artistic detail.

criteria.description: Represents and names a river.
Represents and names the sea.

questions.stem: A child draws a tree and says, 'I created this tree.' Explain the difference between the drawing and the tree it shows.
hints: Ask which thing is on paper and which thing grows.
questions.explanation: Separate a representation from its subject. The child made the drawing; the tree is the creation named in the religious lesson.

criteria.description: Distinguishes the drawing from a real tree.
Says the child made the drawing.
Connects the real tree to the curriculum teaching.

questions.stem: Make a short spoken rhyme about three different creations in our lesson. Name each clearly.
hints: Choose your three names before making the rhyme.
questions.explanation: Select three curriculum examples. Include them in a short recitation; exact rhyming is not required for content marks.

criteria.description: Includes three distinct listed creations.
Communicates the names clearly in a short recitation.

questions.stem: Design a small chart showing one human being, one animal and one water feature. Name each and tell why the chart fits our lesson.
hints: Plan three parts, then explain their shared connection.
questions.explanation: Represent the three categories. Explain that all are examples named in the curriculum.

criteria.description: Represents and names a human being, an animal and a river or sea.
Connects the chart to the lesson about God's creations.

questions.stem: Your group can show only four pictures about this lesson. Choose four different listed creations and explain your choices.
hints: Check that your choices are different and appear in the lesson.
questions.explanation: Select four distinct curriculum examples. Explain how they illustrate the topic.

criteria.description: Names four different examples from humankind, animals, trees, rivers, sea and mountains.
Explains that the choices show things the lesson teaches God created.

uncertain: Content-standard code BI is retained as printed.

indicators.content_standard_as_printed: BI. 1.1.1. Explain who the Creator is

skills.description: Recognise love, truthfulness, kindness, patience and mercy in curriculum examples.
Connect attributes to caring actions at home, school and in the community.
Explain or role-play caring actions that illustrate the attributes.

misconceptions: Patience is confused with pushing ahead
Truthfulness is confused with hiding a mistake
Mercy is confused with excusing continued harm

questions.stem: Which quality is an attribute discussed in this lesson?
hints: Choose the quality shown by caring for someone.
questions.explanation: Kindness is named in the curriculum. The other choices do not express the caring attributes taught here.

questions.stem: Which word means telling the truth?
hints: Look for the word connected to truth.
questions.explanation: Truthfulness means being truthful. It is one of the attributes named in the lesson.

distractor_misconceptions.0: Boasting is mistaken for honest speech
distractor_misconceptions.2: Teasing is mistaken for honest speech

questions.stem: Which quality helps a child wait calmly for a turn?
hints: Think about calm waiting.
questions.explanation: Waiting calmly illustrates patience. Patience is listed in the curriculum.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Wanting everything first is confused with patience
distractor_misconceptions.3: Rudeness is confused with calm waiting

questions.stem: Name the attribute beginning with 'l' that family members show when they care for one another.
hints: Think about caring deeply for others.
questions.explanation: The curriculum connects caring with love. Love is the requested attribute.

questions.stem: Which word is also named among the attributes in our lesson?
hints: Choose the word associated with compassionate treatment.
questions.explanation: Mercy is explicitly listed. Revenge, bullying and jealousy are not the caring attributes taught here.

questions.stem: Ama helps a family member carry a light bag safely. Which attribute does this action show?
hints: Think about helpful care.
questions.explanation: Ama gives safe help. This is an example of kindness at home.

distractor_misconceptions.2: A caring act is confused with dishonesty
distractor_misconceptions.3: Helpful care is confused with mockery

questions.stem: Kojo breaks a pencil by accident and tells the teacher what happened. Which attribute does he show?
hints: Focus on what he says about the accident.
questions.explanation: Kojo honestly reports his mistake. His speech illustrates truthfulness.

distractor_misconceptions.3: Reporting a mistake is confused with impatience

questions.stem: Esi waits calmly while her classmate finishes speaking. Which attribute fits best?
hints: Focus on her calm waiting.
questions.explanation: Esi lets another child finish without rushing them. This illustrates patience at school.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Respectful waiting is confused with cruelty

questions.stem: Name one safe action that shows care for a family member at home.
hints: Think of a small helpful act you can manage.
questions.explanation: Choose a safe action suited to a child. Explain how it helps the family member.

criteria.description: Names a safe and appropriate helpful action.
Connects the action to care, love or kindness.

questions.stem: A new child feels lonely at school. Suggest one action that shows love or kindness.
hints: Think about helping someone feel welcome.
questions.explanation: Consider the child's feeling. Suggest an inclusive action and connect it to kindness.

criteria.description: Suggests a welcoming action such as inviting the child to join a suitable activity.
Explains that the action shows care.

questions.stem: Your teacher describes a supervised visit to comfort sick people. Which attributes could such care show? Name two.
hints: Think about the lesson's caring qualities.
questions.explanation: Connect comforting people with the listed attributes. Several caring qualities may be illustrated.

criteria.description: Names two appropriate listed attributes such as love, kindness or mercy.
Links them to comforting or caring for people.

questions.stem: A classmate admits a small mistake and wants to put it right. Describe a merciful response.
hints: Think of a kind response that still allows the mistake to be corrected.
questions.explanation: Respond compassionately. Mercy can include helping someone correct a mistake without humiliating them.

criteria.description: Suggests a compassionate response without mockery or revenge.
Allows appropriate correction or help.

questions.stem: With a partner, act out family members caring for one another. Name an attribute your scene shows.
hints: Choose a safe everyday family situation.
questions.explanation: Show a caring action. Explain the attribute illustrated by that action.

criteria.description: Shows a safe helpful family interaction.
Identifies love or kindness and links it to the action.

questions.stem: Act out a child telling the truth about a classroom mistake. Show one helpful response from the teacher.
hints: Include both the honest statement and a caring reply.
questions.explanation: Show truthfulness in the child's words. Show care through the teacher's response.

criteria.description: Child reports the mistake honestly.
Teacher responds constructively and kindly.
Learner names truthfulness and a caring attribute.

questions.stem: Compare pushing ahead in a queue with waiting calmly. Which action illustrates patience, and why?
hints: Think about respecting other people's turns.
questions.explanation: Compare both actions. Calm waiting respects turns and illustrates patience.

criteria.description: Selects waiting calmly.
Explains how waiting respects others or avoids rushing.

questions.stem: Draw a caring action at school. Explain the action and name the attribute it shows.
hints: Think about helping or welcoming a classmate.
questions.explanation: Represent a caring interaction. Name the attribute and explain the link; artistic skill is not scored.

criteria.description: Explains a suitable school caring action.
Names and links an appropriate listed attribute.

questions.stem: A child mocks someone who made a mistake and calls it kindness. Explain the problem and suggest a kinder action.
hints: Consider how the person feels and what help they need.
questions.explanation: Identify mockery as hurtful. Replace it with an action that shows care.

criteria.description: Explains that mockery can hurt or humiliate.
Suggests supportive help or a respectful response.
Connects the new action to kindness or mercy.

questions.stem: Create a short school scene showing both patience and kindness. Afterwards explain which action shows each attribute.
hints: Plan a waiting moment and a helpful moment.
questions.explanation: Demonstrate two distinct qualities. Explain each through the action that shows it.

criteria.description: Shows a patient action.
Shows a kind action.
Accurately explains the link for each attribute.

questions.stem: A child says, 'I can show kindness only at home.' Give a school example and a community example to explain why the lesson includes more places.
hints: Think about the three settings named in the curriculum.
questions.explanation: The lesson includes home, school and community. Give appropriate examples beyond home.

criteria.description: Gives a suitable school example.
Gives a safe community example, which may be imaginary and adult-supervised.
Explains that caring attributes can be shown in different settings.

questions.stem: Tell a short story in which a child admits a mistake, receives a merciful response and then helps someone. Name the three attributes shown.
hints: Plan the honest words, the compassionate response and the helpful action.
questions.explanation: Connect each part of the story to an attribute. Honest admission shows truthfulness, compassionate treatment shows mercy, and helpful action shows kindness or love.

criteria.description: Includes an honest admission and identifies truthfulness.
Includes a compassionate response and identifies mercy.
Includes a helpful action and identifies kindness or love.
Tells a coherent age-appropriate story.

uncertain: The curriculum lists attributes and illustrative actions but does not provide a theological definition of each attribute; questions assess the listed qualities and observable actions.
Content-standard code BI is retained as printed.

coverage_note: The previous inventory totals of 78 indicators and 1560 questions have not been independently revalidated in this part. This file covers only the two indicator codes explicitly included above.
